direction.direction:
We keep the garden exactly as it looks now (same chunky simplified forms, same dusk palette, same dark value range, the maple as the only hot accent) and add character as designed, drawn-on-purpose elements, built from real 3D geometry plus real normal maps. I checked your question: the garden had NO normal maps (175 Bump nodes only), and none of its 132 mesh objects had a UV map, so every builder must also write UV maps. I wrote and tested a small helper for making normal maps with a test light (it also caught a Blender 5.2.2 trap where changing the colour space after writing pixels turns the image black).

Element by element. WOOD: follow the bridge sheet and the plank sheet. Rebuild the bridge as it would really be built: flat footing stones in the water, square posts, cross beams, stringers, planks laid across with round pegs, a few iron cramps, a diagonal board at each turn, no span over 1.4 m. The old bridge floated on four small stone blocks and six thin sticks, with plank runs poking through each other. Every plank gets its own width, thickness, bow, rounded worn edges, chipped corners, end splits, gaps, a few replaced boards; moss and mould only near water, posts and shade. The veranda deck sat inside the stone plinth with only 1 cm showing, so the plinth is lowered and the boards get real thickness, staggered butt joints, a nosing and nail heads. ROOF: follow the roof and lantern sheets. Tile-to-tile colour, slipped, chipped and missing tiles, soft moss in the valleys, pale lichen, drip stains under the eave, ridge-end caps, eave discs, stained plaster walls with few clean cracks and loss patches, one soft moss cap on each big rock, a wet band at the waterline, cracked lantern with a chipped cap. GROUND: follow the grass sheet. Ten tuft shapes in clumps, some with seed heads, a few small flowers, soft moss cushions, worn bare paths, a soil lip at the gravel kerb, moss collars at rock feet, leaf litter. POND AND TREES: follow the pond and tree sheets. Clear shallow edge over pebbles and a dark deeper middle, ripples as a normal map, notched lily pads with flowers, iris and cattails, floating red leaves, a green rim at the waterline, the maple as 5 to 8 layered pads with branches showing, the pine as flat discs on a plated trunk.

What we will NOT copy: dark outline strokes, the turquoise water and flat cartoon look of one pass, a moon in the sky, posts standing up like railings, long wide scan-like planks, fuzzy photographic moss, hair-like grass or a meadow, glossy wet streaks, the leafy photographic hedge, the yellow ground drift, the deep-red maple shift, big bright roof moss tufts. Of the six swatches only the plaster one is used as a texture; the plank one gives marks only; the roof, grass, moss-scale and pond-bed ones are rejected (the pond-bed one even has a blurred copy of the whole garden in its lower part). None of the concept pictures is pasted on.

Guard against realism: keep the measured value range (hero median 0.32, 99 percent at most 0.92, saturation 0.36 to 0.44), keep detail energy between 0.9 and 1.4 times today and never above 10, soft large-scale normal maps only. No image money was spent in this step; about 18 seconds of card time were used.

About "nothing running": for about 50 minutes (07:37 to 08:30 UTC) the RunPod render service accepted my jobs but never started them. Its health page showed jobs waiting and graphics cards "idle". RunPod's public status page said all services were fine. I cancelled my own three waiting jobs and sent a fresh one, and that one ran at 08:30. I don't know what fixed it. While it was stuck I did the checks that need no graphics card on this computer (the conflict check, run twice, and small CPU test pictures). All of that is now repeated or superseded on the card.

What I did, in order:
1. Chained the four stages on the starting scene (wood, roof, ground, pond). The starting scene is never saved over.
2. Checked after every stage that it touched only what it owns: objects, materials, node groups, collections, lights and light links, cameras, world, compositor, render settings. 3. Saved garden_character.blend on the store (81 MB, all pictures packed inside). I re-opened the saved file and re-checked every normal map; it draws the same 3,987,764 triangles as before saving.

Four close-ups at 1600 x 1067 were drawn the same way (about 17 to 24 s each).
7. Made the four sheets for you.

Short verdict: the picture keeps the same composition, palette, dusk light and the maple as the single hot accent. GROUND FIX ROUND, all five items done, one thing partly (the squint test). I copied the builder's ground stage and its modules into the fix/ground folder, changed only the copies, and tested it on RunPod: alone, over the combined garden, and inside a full rebuild (wood, roof, this ground stage, pond, final) from the starting scene.

ITEM BY ITEM
(1) Tufts: FIXED. They are now chunky: 4 to 6 broad folded leaves per tuft (3.5 to 9 cm wide, soft tips, lighter vein, darker edge) instead of 6 to 9 thin blades 6 to 14 mm wide; plump pale seed heads on three-sided stalks (the old flat stalks vanished edge-on and left heads floating, which I found and fixed); colours pulled toward grey so sunlit blades stay olive. Same 12 shapes and 16 meshes, same clumps, 499 to 511 tufts instead of about 616, 22 percent with seed heads. Evidence: the lineup picture, the 100 percent crops on the sheet.
(2) Moss cushions: FIXED. Sizes now vary 0.6 to 1.5 times the old size (the spread from small to big is about 4 to 1), a third fewer in the veranda bank (536 cushions there before, 354 now, about 66 percent), six soft domes with no pinched crease (a third are plain round domes), low moss mats between touching cushions, and every cushion has its own tone. The bank now reads as uneven moss, not rows of bean bags. The carpet effect is modest: the mats are mostly hidden under the domes.
(3) Worn path: FIXED. One soft bare-earth shape with no grass islands or camouflage blotches, a lighter dusty middle, a damper darker rim, soft slow and fine blotches, and 19 real little pebbles (3 to 6 cm). The veranda patch has the same modelling. Small leftover: a wedge of lawn still pokes into the path in the 45 degree close-up.
(4) Flowers and fallen leaves: FIXED. 24 five-petal flowers (6.4 to 8 cm across) in four short curved lines, 11 to 32 pixels wide at 2400 px; 36 five-pointed red maple stars 14 to 20 cm across, 22 to 76 px wide. Flowers cover 0.11 percent of the hero and 0.28 percent of the veranda (limit 0.3).
(5) Lawn: FIXED. Gentle two-scale olive and warm-brown mottling (neutral on average), ground normal map 15 percent softer, and a little litter: 20 twigs, 33 dry blades, 16 dry leaves. The lawn no longer looks smeared in the 100 percent crops.

PARTLY: the squint test. Hero 0.883, veranda 0.872 against the previous final; the integrated final had 0.895 and 0.882, so the ground fix lowers it by about 0.01. It is far from 0.92 and cannot reach it from the ground. I ran step-by-step ablations: the chunkier tufts cost 0.011 (hero) and 0.020 (veranda), the moss changes 0.007 and 0.011, the soil and mottling about nothing. The cause is that wide leaves and their long shadows add structure at the 12 pixel blur. Dialling tuft width and density down only bought back 0.001 to 0.009, so I kept the look the person asked for.

CHECKERS' ITEMS: lawn smeared and path flat: fixed (above). Flowers and leaf litter too small: fixed. Moss bank repeat: fixed. Lantern cap moss sticker and neon bands and diamonds on rocks: not mine (roof owner: lantern and rocks). Pegs, drip stains, slipped tiles, bridge, wood, pond, maple, pine: other owners, left alone.
